title: Service contracts, per-model baselines, and regional rescue guidelines
creator: Maya Chen
description: Define a repeatable, per-model service contract framework that (1) establishes baseline SLIs for latency, availability, and correctness per endpoint/model family, (2) encodes progressive degradation policies tied to incremental error-budget burn, and (3) prescribes cross-region rescue/circuit-breaker behaviors and load-shedding thresholds. The goal is to give product teams a clear, auditable SLI/SLO declaration format and operational playbook that the control plane and Console can consume for automated routing/fallback decisions.
acceptance_criteria:
1) A template for per-model service contracts that covers latency P50/P95/P99, success rate, and quality regression indicators.
2) A matrix mapping error-budget burn bands to concrete actions (e.g., autoscale, reject-low-priority, route-to-fallback) including rate limits and priority tiers.
3) A runbook describing regional rescue flow: detection, traffic re-routing, circuit breaker thresholds, and rollback criteria.
4) Prototype JSON schema and example declarations for 3 model families (chat-short, chat-long, embedding).
5) Docs and Console mockups for displaying service-contract state and current error budget consumption.
notes: This ticket bridges product requirements from PM and runtime controls from infra. We need to be careful to not hardcode model-specific constants in the routing layer — prefer profiles with knobs. Work will iterate with Console and Release teams to add visibility. Consider interactions with Dedicated autoscaling policies and Private deployment isolation constraints.
implementation_plan:
Phase 1: Draft SLI taxonomy and 3 example declarations; review with Applied ML and Solutions Eng.
Phase 2: Define degradation bands and circuit-breaker DSL; implement small policy engine prototype in the routing service.
Phase 3: Integrate with Console telemetry to surface live error-budget and allow manual overrides.
Phase 4: Run two-week canary on non-critical routes and gather telemetry for adjustments.
risks:
1) Overly aggressive degradation rules may surface false positives and drop legitimate traffic.
2) Cross-region failover increases egress costs and can introduce higher tail latencies.
3) Private deployments may require opt-out hooks for automated cross-region routing due to regulatory controls.
tradeoffs_considered:
- Strict SLOs vs. progressive degradation: chose graded bands to allow graceful customer-visible behavior.
- Centralized policy engine vs. per-cluster local decisions: prototype central then allow local override in Dedicated/Private.
- Quality SLI (per-prompt regression tests) vs. pure infra metrics: include a lightweight quality signal to avoid blind cost-saving degradations.
